excerpt: It converts any URL to an **LLM-friendly** input with `https://r.jina.ai/https://your.url`.
Behind the scenes, Reader searches the web, fetches the top 5 results, visits each URL, and applies `r.jina.ai` to it.
PDFs and MS Office documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) can now be POSTed directly via the `file` body field — no need to host them first.
All images on a page that lack an `alt` tag can be auto-captioned by a VLM (vision-language model) and formatted as `![Image [idx]: [VLM_caption]](img_URL)`
`x-respond-with` — select the output format. ... `frontmatter` returns **Markdown with a YAML frontmatter block**
`x-preset` — apply a pre-packaged option bundle for common scenarios. ... `research` — for AI research agents needing structured, citable output.
`x-respond-timing` — explicit control over *when* Reader is willing to return. Trade off latency against completeness
A prebuilt image of the open-source branch is published to GitHub Container Registry. It bundles headless Chrome, LibreOffice, and CJK fonts, so you can run Reader without building it yourself.
Route through the SaaS proxy with `-H 'x-proxy: auto'` (key required). Reader's hosted proxy pool rotates residential / datacenter IPs and handles common anti-bot challenges automatically.
Pass your session cookies with the `X-Set-Cookie` header and the Reader forwards them when fetching the URL
Scraping can be complicated and unreliable, particularly with complex or dynamic pages. The Reader API provides a streamlined, reliable output of clean, LLM-ready text.
`x-markdown-chunking` — opt-in semantic chunking of the markdown response. Returns a JSON array (or ``-delimited text) of chunks instead of one blob
Use the `x-json-schema` header with a JSON schema definition, or use `x-instruction` header with natural language instructions. Both features work with ReaderLM-v2 to extract specific fields
